0.7.0.title: Right-click a hole to add a bolt
0.7.0.blurb: Select a hole wall, right-click and choose Add fastener to hole. The size comes from the hole, the length from the material, with an optional washer and nut and a checkbox for all identical holes on the same plane. Everything goes in as separate bodies in one undo step.

0.7.0.title: A Case wizard: a box with a lipped lid in one step
0.7.0.blurb: On the Features tab, Case takes the outside size, wall thickness, corner radius, lid height and the lip (tongue height, width and clearance) and makes the Base and the Lid, with the tongue on one half and a groove on the other.

0.7.0.title: Split body and Lip joint
0.7.0.blurb: Cut a body at a plane into two named bodies, or add a tongue and a groove with a clearance along the cut. The guide builds a two-part case with the volumes checked.

0.7.0.title: Rib with fillet, draft and one-sided thickness
0.7.0.blurb: The Rib editor gains a fillet on the free edge, a draft angle, a choice of side and the bodies it extends to. A rib no longer fills a bore its line runs through.

0.7.0.title: Nut, Standoff and Heat-set insert wizards
0.7.0.blurb: Parametric hex nuts (ISO 4032, 4035, 4033), round and hex standoffs, and heat-set inserts, each with a live preview, from the Features tab. The dimensions are marked unverified until checked against the standards.

0.7.0.title: Patterns in any direction, about any axis
0.7.0.blurb: A linear pattern can run along any direction vector or edge, and a circular pattern about any axis, with a point on the axis, so a bolt circle does not have to sit on the origin.

0.7.0.title: The assistant can measure and check the part
0.7.0.blurb: The Chat and the MCP server can now read distances, clearances, overlaps, wall thickness, draft and manufacturing checks, so an assistant can verify what it built. The injection moulding check also finds undercuts.

0.7.0.title: Script helpers for draft, lip, scale, split and more
0.7.0.blurb: Typed script methods for draft, move face, lip and groove, scale, split, delete body and face, helix, axis, sphere and move body, and sweeps that follow guide curves.

0.6.5.title: Open OBJ, GLB and 3MF files
0.6.5.blurb: Drop or open an .obj, .glb or .3mf file and it is added as a reference mesh, with colours and (for GLB and 3MF) the unit taken from the file. A notice lists what was not read, such as textures and the separate parts of a multi-part file.

0.6.5.title: A Rounded rectangle sketch tool
0.6.5.blurb: Click two corners and the four corners come out rounded. The corner field sets the radius, and a typed radius becomes a dimension on each corner arc; the last radius is kept for the next rectangle. Add spline point inserts a free point on an existing spline.

0.6.4.title: A Spring wizard for compression springs
0.6.4.blurb: On the Features tab, next to Screw and Washer, Spring takes the outside diameter, wire diameter, free length and turns and adds the coil, shows the pitch and the gap between turns and previews it first. Left or right hand, along any axis; a spring() call does the same from a script. The ends are plain wire ends for now.

0.6.4.title: Slotted sheet metal parts from SolidWorks read back in full
0.6.4.blurb: A folded sheet with slots cut through it, such as a chute, no longer stops at an imported remainder with the slots missing. If the sheet cut cannot take a cut, it is applied as a plain cut and the feature row says so.

0.6.4.title: A second propeller no longer lands on the first
0.6.4.blurb: The Marine propeller wizard has a Position along the shaft setting, starts a new propeller behind the ones already in the part, and warns before inserting an identical one at the same place.

0.6.3.title: Chat: ask for a change in words
0.6.3.blurb: The new Chat panel runs the Claude Code you already have on your own computer. Describe a part or a change, watch it build in the open document, and undo the whole edit in one step. It is off until you start the local service and link the app.

0.6.3.title: Document tabs, right-click menus and a one-row sketch bar
0.6.3.blurb: Open parts are tabs in the top bar. Right-click a feature, a plane, a tab or an open sketch for the commands you expect there, and the sketch bar now stays on one row.

0.6.3.title: Midpoint guides and value boxes that grow with a formula
0.6.3.blurb: While you draw, the pointer also lines up with the middle of an existing line, and with two midpoints it lands where their dotted guides cross. The length, angle and radius boxes widen as you type a formula such as =width*2+wall.

0.6.1.title: Roughness, metalness, clear coat and wood grain
0.6.1.blurb: The Display menu's Surface group sets how a part catches the light, and draws a wood grain with the ring spacing, contrast and colour you choose.

0.6.1.title: Textures from Poly Haven
0.6.1.blurb: Pick a wood texture from the free Poly Haven library in the Display menu and the part is drawn with it, with roughness, a size slider and the author credited. Online libraries are off until you allow them.

0.6.1.title: Choose the mass unit and digits
0.6.1.blurb: Settings > General > Mass display shows a mass in grams, kilograms, pounds or ounces with 3 to 6 digits, everywhere a mass appears.

0.6.0.title: A fold can cross a window
0.6.0.blurb: A fold line through a window or hole of a sheet metal part now bends the part and cuts the window through the bend.

0.6.0.title: Delete both
0.6.0.blurb: Delete something others use and the notice names what depends on it, with a Delete both button that removes them together in one step.

0.6.0.title: The BOM as plain text
0.6.0.blurb: Copy as text and Save as text give the bill of materials as aligned columns, ready for an e-mail, next to Save CSV.

0.6.0.title: More woods and panels
0.6.0.blurb: Birch, cedar, cherry, Douglas fir, eucalyptus, maple, teak and walnut join the Material list, each with its own colour, density and source.

0.6.0.title: A Washer wizard
0.6.0.blurb: Pick a flat or spring washer size from ISO 7089, ISO 7093-1 or DIN 127 B, or type your own, and it lands in the tree as one folder.

0.5.0.title: A Sheet metal tab
0.5.0.blurb: Convert a solid to sheet, add edge flanges, hems and corner reliefs, cut across bends and round or chamfer corners. Edge flange, Hem and Corner open with their pick list ready: tap the edges or corners in the model, tap again to take one out.

0.5.0.title: Flanges on part of an edge, with shaped legs
0.5.0.blurb: An edge flange can cover the whole edge, a start and length along it, or the span between two points you pick, with shaped legs, holes and relief. Bases with rounded corners take flanges too.

0.5.0.title: SolidWorks sheet metal opens as editable sheet metal
0.5.0.blurb: Open an SLDPRT sheet metal part and its flanges come back as editable Edge flange features, with partial-width and sketched-profile flanges, leg rounds, slots and holes.

0.5.0.title: Arc slot
0.5.0.blurb: A curved slot in the sketch tools: pick the centre, the start of the slot and its end, then set the radius and width.

0.5.0.title: Dimension to the part's own edge
0.5.0.blurb: With the Dimension tool, click an outer edge of the part to set how far a slot or hole sits from it.

0.5.0.title: Library
0.5.0.blurb: Samples is now Library: every library in one picker, a Manage libraries list, pictures on saved parts, and Insert into this part on each card.

0.5.0.title: One filter for the Library
0.5.0.blurb: A category menu and tags with counts narrow the Library cards, and Clear brings everything back.
